items.title: Joe Robichaux Interview, 1959-03-19
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well it would be too late at that. So didn't Professor Oakeshore live uptown for a while on Camp Street? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, he used to live on Camp Street. Well he stayed on Camp Street practically all his life.

ctx.x: And I was living uptown and I came back two days after he was up and he had a few chickens and he was out there in the yard feeding the chickens and he was all right. And he had been very little sick and I didn't think that he was going to make it then. And so anyway, he got all right and he was up. So I went out of town because I used to go and see him, used to be down there four, sometimes five times a week. I used to come down and see him and sit down and talk. So finally when I left and went off this time, he…
Well it would be too late at that. So didn't Professor Oakeshore live uptown for a while on Camp Street?

Yeah, he used to live on Camp Street. Well he stayed on Camp Street practically all his life. He stayed up there until his wife died, see after his wife died, well that's where he moved downtown after that and then he remarried and remarried again. And then he remarried again, well then he stayed down here and then he sold the house up on Camp Street. Well they was living at 611 and he moved from 611, I believe he died there and then my aunt moved from 611 and she bought a house 920 Oysalon and that's where she…
